skill.name: azure-resource-manager-playwright-dotnet
skill.description: Guides .NET developers through Azure Resource Manager operations for Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces. It covers provisioning, updates, deletion, quotas, name availability, and authentication with Azure SDK clients.
skill.summary: Manage Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces with the Azure Resource Manager .NET SDK.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Azure Playwright Testing management needs precise ARM SDK patterns. This skill provides focused .NET guidance for workspace lifecycle, quotas, and name checks.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup for Azure.ResourceManager.Playwright and Azure.Identity.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and ArmClient setup for Azure management calls.
Demonstrates create, get, list, update, and delete workflows for Playwright workspaces.
Covers workspace name availability checks and quota retrieval.
Summarizes key SDK types, workspace properties, and common error handling.
Links to Microsoft documentation for API reference and Playwright Testing overview.
limitations: It does not run Playwright tests or configure test execution projects.
It does not verify live Azure permissions, subscription state, or quota availability.
Examples assume an authenticated Azure environment and an existing resource group.
Version details may need checking against NuGet before production use.

use_cases.title: Provision Playwright Testing workspaces
use_cases.description: Create or update Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces through Azure Resource Manager in .NET applications.

use_cases.title: Prepare test platform infrastructure
use_cases.description: Inspect workspace IDs, service URLs, quotas, and names before connecting automated browser tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize ARM automation guidance
use_cases.description: Use consistent SDK types, authentication patterns, and error handling in internal Azure automation docs.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the right SDK
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner selection between management and test execution packages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when to use Azure.ResourceManager.Playwright instead of the Playwright test execution SDK in a .NET project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a workspace plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft the steps to create a Microsoft Playwright Testing workspace with the Azure Resource Manager .NET SDK.

prompt_templates.title: Review quota and naming flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET workflow that checks workspace name availability and reads subscription and workspace quotas.

prompt_templates.title: Design lifecycle automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ARM SDK strategy for creating, updating, tagging, listing, and deleting Playwright Testing workspaces safely.

output_examples.input: I need a new Playwright Testing workspace in West US 3.
output_examples.output: A concise management plan that installs the SDK, authenticates with Azure Identity, creates the workspace, and records the service URL.

output_examples.input: I need to check a workspace name and review quotas first.
output: The response separates subscription name checks from quota reads.
It identifies the relevant ARM resource types and expected status fields.
It notes that live Azure permissions and quota limits must be verified in the target subscription.

output_examples.input: I am documenting how developers should manage these workspaces.
output_examples.output: A structured outline covering authentication, resource hierarchy, workspace lifecycle operations, quota handling, and Microsoft documentation links.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and avoid hardcoded secrets in examples and automation.
Check name availability and quotas before provisioning new workspaces.
Handle Azure RequestFailedException cases for conflicts, bad requests, and service errors.
anti_patterns: Using this management SDK as if it runs Playwright tests.
Embedding tenant IDs, client IDs, or client secrets directly in source files.
Skipping long-running operation handling when creating or deleting workspaces.

faq.question: Does this skill run Playwright tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure Resource Manager operations for Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces.

faq.question: Which .NET package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.ResourceManager.Playwright for management plane operations.

faq.question: Can it help create a workspace?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes the SDK flow for creating or updating a Playwright Testing workspace.

faq.question: Does it explain Azure authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses DefaultAzureCredential with ArmClient for Azure management calls.

faq.question: Can it inspect quotas?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers subscription-level and workspace-level quota lookup patterns.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production automation?
faq.answer: It can guide production automation, but teams must verify permissions, regions, quotas, and package versions.
